setup: fp32 AdamW, lr 1e-5 + 50 warmup, grad-ckpt off, activation-quant off, no autocast, QAT-only freeze
interpretation: Zero-shot floor: binary 100.0, ternary 140.8 WER (naive binarize pretrained).
Constant alpha=1 QAT: binary WER non-monotone (434->99->104->191), ends WORSE than the floor; fp16 readout stays clean (2.62).
Alpha-ramp QAT: loss reaches 1.02 (lower than full precision ~3.6) yet alpha=1 WER stays ~70-250%; fp16 readout is CORRUPTED (10.30 vs 2.62).

Low teacher-forced loss with ~100% generation WER indicates the failure is NOT a simple recovery problem; likely a train/eval (teacher-forced vs autoregressive) mismatch and/or that binarizing decoder attention fundamentally breaks generation.
The alpha-ramp is confirmed as a corruption trigger (ramp fp16 10.30 vs constant fp16 2.62).
Per the agreed criterion (flat/worse WER), treat as a BUG, not recovery.
next_steps: Decisive generation test: after QAT, greedily generate on a TRAINING utterance and check whether it reproduces the label; if not, it is a quantized-forward/generation bug.
Compare quantized forward logits (teacher-forced) vs generated tokens to locate the divergence.
Finish trigger isolation: gradient checkpointing, then activation quant (alpha-ramp already confirmed).
Investigate per-layer scale handling for attention projections in the full model (per-tensor centered-sign may be too coarse); try group-wise and/or exclude attention from binarization.
